tally.headline: 1 of 3 gradeable claims held up, 2 did not

implied_side.book: captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers
implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 6.1 points toward Fresno State of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 48.8 sat 0.3 points above the captured total of 48.5.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 1 of 1 gradeable claims held up and none was contradicted. The game was decided by the things EdgeDesk said would decide it.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 0.1 and the game finished 7 the away way — 7.1 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

verdict.line: The number did not land and the reasoning did. That is the case a bettor should be least upset about: the read was defensible and the distribution went the other way. Nothing here needs changing yet.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 2 published claims said the same thing: EdgeDesk makes it Fresno State -0.1 where the market has Fresno State +6.0 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers — a 6.1 points disagreement. EdgeDesk prices this game at Fresno State -0.1 with a fair total of 47.8, which makes Fresno State the better team here by that margin on this field.
lessons.actual_result: Fresno State Bulldogs lost by 7. Fresno State Bulldogs lost by 7 where EdgeDesk projected a 0.1-point edge.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk named Fresno State as better in market and the game went the other way, across 2 separate published claims. One game does not overturn a season-long rating, but this is the direction to watch: the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.suggested_investigation: These claims carried 6.2 points of the published number between them and were contradicted. Check whether the same category has been contradicted in other games this season before touching anything.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 8 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, matchup.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.actual_result: It graded a loss, and the reasoning held up: 1 of 1 gradeable claims held up and none was contradicted. The game was decided by the things EdgeDesk said would decide it.
lessons.lesson: A losing number on a read the game supported. This is the result type that should change the least. Over-correcting on it is how a defensible process gets thrown away for a distribution doing what distributions do.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 48.8.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 69 points, an error of 20.2.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk makes it Fresno State -0.1 where the market has Fresno State +6.0 at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at BetRivers — a 6.1 points disagreement.
lessons.actual_result: Fresno State Bulldogs lost by 7. the result landed on the market’s side of the disagreement
lessons.lesson: The market had the better estimate here. EdgeDesk’s disagreement was not information on this game, and the honest reading is that the price already contained what the model thought it had found.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Track disagreements of this size across the season. The question is not whether one landed; it is whether the class of them has any edge at all.
